chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān and Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Layth al-Murādī, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿUtbah al-Hāshimī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man whose garment falls upon the water with which istinjāʾ was performed: does that make his garment impure? He said: “No.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.اسْتَنْجَى بِهِ: used for istinjāʾ, cleansing after relieving oneself
key_terms.لَا: a direct negation indicating the ruling is no

ai.seo_question: Does water used for istinjāʾ make clothing impure if it touches it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity. It states that if a garment comes into contact with the water used for istinjāʾ, that contact does not render the garment impure.
